the sympathetic nervous system is activated in essential hypertension, but the degree of activation varies among different patients, with the greatest activation occurring in the young.

in essential hypertension, sympathetic nervous system activity is increased, especially in younger patients, and that increased renal and, to a lesser extent, cardiac noradrenalne release accounts for most of this.
the sympathetic nervous system is activated early and to a large extent in essential hypertension, but the extent of the increase is age-dependent and the mechanism is complex.

the pathophysiologic role of increased sympathetic nervous system activity in the genesis of essential hypertension, a condition that affects approximately one in five adults and is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
the role of the sympathetic nervous system in the pathogenesis and treatment of human essential hypertension.
the mechanisms of essential hypertension.

the elevated plasma norepinephrine concentration in essential hypertension results from an increased rate of norepinephine release to plasma, and that the increase is due to increased activity of the sympathetic nervous system.

increased sympathetic nervous system activity is a common pathophysiologic feature of essential hypertension.
